questions.question: How much paid time off do full-time staff earn each month?
questions.answer: Full-time employees accrue 1.75 days of paid time off for every month of service, which adds up to 21 days per year [1].

questions.question: Can I keep unused vacation days for next year, and until when?
questions.answer: You may carry over up to 8 unused PTO days into the next calendar year [2]. Unused sick days do not carry over and are not paid out [3].

questions.question: How far in advance must I request more than five consecutive days off?
questions.answer: Requests for more than five consecutive days must be submitted at least three weeks in advance [1].

questions.question: How many paid sick days do employees get per year?
questions.answer: Employees receive 12 paid sick days per calendar year [1].

questions.question: When do I need to show a medical certificate for being ill?
questions.answer: If you are sick for more than three consecutive working days, you must provide a doctor's note to HR [3]. Please tell your manager as early as possible on the first day you are unwell [3].

questions.question: How long is parental leave for the primary caregiver?
questions.answer: The primary caregiver receives 18 weeks of fully paid parental leave [1].

questions.question: Is there a gentler schedule after returning from having a baby?
questions.answer: The secondary caregiver receives 6 weeks of fully paid leave, which can be taken any time within the first year after the birth or adoption [1]. Employees returning from parental leave may work a reduced 80 percent schedule at full pay for their first month back [1].

questions.question: How many days a week can I work from home?
questions.answer: Employees may work remotely up to three days per week [1]. Our standard working week is 38 hours [2].

questions.question: Will the company pay for my desk and chair at home?
questions.answer: New remote workers receive a one-time home office stipend of 400 euros for a desk, chair or monitor [1].

questions.question: Can I work from another country for a few weeks?
questions.answer: Working from another country for more than 20 working days per year requires approval from the People team because of tax and insurance rules [1].

questions.question: Within how many days must expense claims be submitted in Ledgerly?
questions.answer: Submit expense claims within 30 days of the purchase through Ledgerly, our expense tool, and attach a receipt for every item [1].

questions.question: How much can I spend on food per day on a business trip?
questions.answer: Meals while travelling are covered up to 45 euros per day [2].

questions.question: Is there money for training courses and conferences?
questions.answer: Every employee has an annual learning budget of 1,200 euros for courses, books and conference tickets [1].

questions.question: What is the minimum password length?
questions.answer: All passwords must be at least 14 characters long [1].

questions.question: What second factor do administrators have to use?
questions.answer: Administrators must use a hardware security key as their second factor; authenticator apps are not sufficient for admin access [1].

questions.question: I left my work laptop on the train. How quickly do I have to tell someone?
questions.answer: If a laptop or phone with company data is lost or stolen, report it to security@northwind.example within one hour so the device can be wiped remotely [1]. If you work more than 45 hours in a week because of an incident or a launch, record it in the HR portal and take the equivalent time back within the next two months [3].

questions.question: After how many minutes of inactivity must screens lock?
questions.answer: Screens must lock automatically after five minutes of inactivity [1].

questions.question: How often do managers check who still needs system permissions?
questions.answer: Managers review the system access of their team members every quarter [1].

questions.question: How quickly must critical vulnerabilities be patched?
questions.answer: Critical vulnerabilities must be patched within 7 days of disclosure [1]. High-severity vulnerabilities must be patched within 30 days, and medium-severity ones within 90 days [1].

questions.question: How often are simulated phishing exercises run?
questions.answer: We also run a simulated phishing exercise every month; anyone who clicks a simulated phishing link is enrolled in a short refresher course [1].

questions.question: Which HTTP header carries the API key?
questions.answer: Every request must include an API key [1].

questions.question: After I rotate a key, how long does the old one keep working?
questions.answer: The old key keeps working for 24 hours after a rotation so that deployments can be updated without downtime [1].

questions.question: What is the rate limit on the Growth plan?
questions.answer: Rate limits depend on your plan [1]. The Growth plan costs 12 US dollars per user per month, billed annually [2].

questions.question: What should my client do when the API says I'm sending too many requests?
questions.answer: When you exceed the limit the API responds with HTTP status 429 and a Retry-After header that tells you how many seconds to wait before retrying [1]. Every request must include an API key [2].

questions.question: What does error NW-4012 mean?
questions.answer: Error code NW-1001 means the API key is missing or invalid [1]. Error code NW-4012 means a webhook signature did not match the payload [1].

questions.question: I'm getting NW-2003. What is wrong?
questions.answer: Error code NW-2003 means the monthly quota for your plan has been exhausted [1].

questions.question: What is the maximum page size for list endpoints?
questions.answer: The maximum page size is 200 items and the default is 50 [1].

questions.question: How many times are failed webhooks retried, and how is each delivery signed?
questions.answer: Webhook deliveries that fail are retried 8 times over 24 hours with exponential backoff [1].

questions.question: How long is an old API version supported after it is deprecated?
questions.answer: The API is versioned by date, for example 2026-01-15 [1]. Breaking changes are only released in a new version, and deprecated versions are supported for 12 months after the deprecation notice [1].

questions.question: What uptime does Northwind commit to for Enterprise customers?
questions.answer: Northwind commits to a monthly uptime of 99.95 percent for Enterprise customers and 99.9 percent for Growth customers [1].

questions.question: What service credit do I get if monthly availability was 97 percent?
questions.answer: Uptime below 99.95 percent but at least 99.0 percent earns a credit of 10 percent of the monthly fee [1]. Uptime below 99.0 percent but at least 95.0 percent earns a 25 percent credit [1].

questions.question: Is there a deadline to ask for money back after an outage month?
questions.answer: If monthly uptime falls below the commitment, customers receive a credit on the next invoice [1]. Credits must be claimed through the support portal within 30 days after the end of the affected month [1]. Error code NW-5000 indicates an internal server error; these are safe to retry with exponential backoff [4].

questions.question: What is the first response time for P1 incidents on Enterprise?
questions.answer: Enterprise customers can raise P1 incidents 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, and receive a first response within 15 minutes [1].

questions.question: When does planned downtime for upgrades happen?
questions.answer: Customers are notified at least 72 hours in advance, and planned maintenance does not count as downtime [1].

questions.question: What counts as a SEV1 incident?
questions.answer: Every SEV1 and SEV2 incident has an Incident Commander who coordinates the response and makes decisions, a Communications Lead who updates customers and stakeholders, and a Scribe who keeps a timeline in the incident channel [1]. For SEV1 incidents the status page must be updated within 15 minutes of the incident being declared, and then at least every 30 minutes until it is resolved [2]. A written postmortem is required for every SEV1 and SEV2 incident and must be published within 5 business days [4].

questions.question: How long does the on-call engineer have to respond to an urgent page?
questions.answer: For a SEV1, page the primary on-call engineer immediately through PagerBell [1]. If the page is not acknowledged within 10 minutes, PagerBell escalates automatically to the secondary on-call and then to the engineering manager [1]. On-call engineers receive a weekly allowance and an extra day off after a week with night pages [2].

questions.question: How often must the status page be updated during a SEV1?
questions.answer: For SEV1 incidents the status page must be updated within 15 minutes of the incident being declared, and then at least every 30 minutes until it is resolved [1].

questions.question: By when does the write-up after a major outage need to be published?
questions.answer: A written postmortem is required for every SEV1 and SEV2 incident and must be published within 5 business days [1].

questions.question: How much does the Growth plan cost?
questions.answer: The Growth plan costs 12 US dollars per user per month, billed annually [1].

questions.question: Where is European customer data hosted?
questions.answer: Customers can choose where their data is stored [1].

questions.question: In which formats can workspace data be exported?
questions.answer: Workspace owners can export all data at any time as CSV, JSON or Parquet files from the settings page [1].

questions.question: What happens to my data if I stop paying and close my account?
questions.answer: We fulfil data subject requests under the GDPR, such as access or erasure, within 30 days [1]. Restricted data, such as customer payment details and health information, may only be accessed with written approval from the data owner [2]. Data never leaves the selected region except for encrypted backups, which are kept in a second region on the same continent [5].

questions.question: Which plan includes SAML single sign-on?
questions.answer: SAML single sign-on and SCIM user provisioning are available on the Enterprise plan only [1].

questions.question: For how long are database backups kept?
questions.answer: Database backups are taken daily and kept for 35 days [1].

questions.question: How long are audit logs retained on the Enterprise plan?
questions.answer: Audit logs are retained for 1 year by default and for 7 years on the Enterprise plan [1].

questions.question: How quickly do you handle a request to delete my personal data?
questions.answer: We fulfil data subject requests under the GDPR, such as access or erasure, within 30 days [1]. After cancellation your data is kept for 30 days so that you can reactivate or export it, and then it is permanently deleted [3].

questions.question: Can I ship to production on Friday afternoon?
questions.answer: We deploy to production from Monday to Thursday [1].

questions.question: How many approvals does a pull request to main need?
questions.answer: Every pull request to the main branch needs approval from two reviewers, and at least one of them must be a code owner of the changed files [1]. Keep pull requests under 400 changed lines where possible; large changes are hard to review well [1].
